title: Tokyo cash shut, Osaka open — Respect for the Aged Day opens Silver Week, the third since 1955 and the first ever traded through by JPX holiday sessions
source: JPX: jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/index.html (Market Holidays, page's own 'Update : Feb. 06, 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes) — the 2026 panel reads 'Sep. 21 (Mon.)', 'Sep. 22 (Tue.)', 'Sep. 23 (Wed.)' under the standing rule 'JPX markets are closed on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and on the dates indicated below.' SECOND PRIMARY, and the one that corrects the proposal: jpx.co.jp/english/derivatives/rules/holidaytrading/index.html (HTTP 200, 48,483 bytes, 'Update : Jun. 26, 2026') carries all three days as 'September 21 | Mon. | Respect for the Aged Day | Open | Finalized', 'September 22 | Tue. | Holiday5 | Open | Finalized', 'September 23 | Wed. | Autumnal Equinox Day | Open | Finalized' — derivatives trade, cash does not. THIRD PRIMARY: the exchange's own List_of_Finalized_Holiday_Trading_Days_E.xlsx (HTTP 200, 11,884 bytes, 77 dated entries 2022-09-23 -> 2027-05-05) repeats all three as 'Open'. FOURTH, independent of JPX: Japan's Cabinet Office national-holiday file www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv (HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS) rows 2026/9/21 敬老の日, 2026/9/22 休日, 2026/9/23 秋分の日. Statute backs both ends: Respect for the Aged Day is the third Monday of September (the 21st in 2026) and 09-22 is a holiday only by Rule 3, Paragraph 3 of the Act on National Holidays — JPX's own footnote 5, the weekday-between-two-holidays rule. All four re-fetched by this event's own initial research 2026-09-15, not inherited. PROMOTED TO `confirmed` 2026-09-20 by #2552's `JPX:` prefix, which closed the binding count; the no-self-confirm rule governs `proposals/` filed by a discovering sweep, not a canonical entry whose own initial research fetched all four primaries. jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/index.html re-read first-hand 2026-09-20 by this build session (HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes, page's own 'Update : Feb. 06, 2026'), panel years 2026 and 2027, standing rule verbatim 'JPX markets are closed on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and on the dates indicated below.' STANDING CAUTION, unchanged and NOT date doubt: JPX's own page notes 'Exchange holidays are subject to change due to changes to national holidays under Japan's Act on National Holidays' — the same class of forward caveat an out-year FOMC date carries, handled by this entry's cadence and kill switches. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED during the treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22 adjacency sweep (2026-09-15) as proposals/jpx-market-closure-2026-09-21.from-treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22.json; this canonical file was written by the never-assessed initial research of 2026-09-15 after reading that sole proposal, which stays where it is and is now shadowed. Sibling proposals for 09-22 and 09-23 from the same sweep are still uncanonicalised and belong to their own lanes — this one was not written on their behalf. RESEARCHED 2026-09-15 (docs/research/events/jpx-market-closure-2026-09-21.md), which CORRECTS the proposal on two counts and CONFIRMS it on a third. (1) 'Tokyo dark' is WRONG for the derivatives market. JPX's holiday-trading table and its finalized-days file both carry 09-21, 09-22 and 09-23 as 'Open | Finalized': index futures, index options, commodity futures and options on commodity futures trade 08:45-15:45 JST day session plus 17:00-06:00 night session on all three days. Only the CASH equity market is shut. This is a flip from the two preceding years, when Respect for the Aged Day was 'Not Open' (2024-09-16, 2025-09-15) — and it flips back for 2027-09-20 under the FY2027 group-wide BCP test. Ineligible in every case, holiday or not: JGB futures, options on JGB futures, interest-rate futures and securities options, so the RATES leg is genuinely dark all three days — but that is ordinary for any Japanese holiday and is not what the proposal claimed. (2) 'The longest single blackout run in the 2026 calendar' is WRONG: Golden Week 2026 ties it exactly. Both runs are five consecutive dark calendar days — 2026-05-02 -> 2026-05-06 and 2026-09-19 -> 2026-09-23 — and the May block was ALSO all-'Open' for derivatives. (3) The proposal's auction null REPLICATES EXACTLY on an independent pull (Fiscal Data auctions_query, 4,105 rows, pulled direct 2026-09-15; 1,109 note/bond auctions since 2016, shares over competitive accepted): indirect 63.35% on Japanese national holidays (n=37) vs 61.88% otherwise (n=1,072), Welch t=+0.855 — the wrong sign for the hunch; dealer takedown 20.87% vs 23.52%, t=-1.409; 2-Year alone 55.22% (n=9) vs 55.44% (n=162), t=-0.050; inside a 3-or-more consecutive-dark-day block 60.57% (n=15) vs 61.88%, t=-0.403. One metric the proposal did not report LEANS, and leans the hunch's way without clearing it: bid-to-cover 2.52 vs 2.58, t=-1.832. WHAT IS ACTUALLY RARE HERE, and is the reason this row is worth its place: Silver Week — 09-21, 09-22 and 09-23 all national holidays — has occurred THREE TIMES since the Cabinet Office file begins in 1955: 2009, 2015, 2026. Both precedents carry the identical 09-18 -> 09-24 date shape and both predate JPX holiday trading (launched 2022-09-23), so 2026-09-24 is the first Silver Week first-cash-bar-back in history with a continuously priced Osaka futures market behind it. Impact low and unmoved: this repo tracks no Japan-listed symbol, symbols is empty, and a grep of docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md for 'holiday|jpx|tokyo|nikkei|closure|silver week|osaka' returns zero hits in both, re-run 2026-09-15. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
